figure_inventory.description: Two grey rounded panels side by side, each with the same four children standing in a row on a grey oval shadow, labelled under their feet A, B, C, D (left to right), plus a teacher (woman in a sari, holding a clipboard) standing at the left end of the panel, facing the children. LEFT panel (before): teal speech bubble from the teacher: 'Let us play "Statue". Keep turning around ...'. A (boy, khaki shirt, brown shorts, hands raised in front), B (girl, khaki shirt, brown skirt), C (boy), D (girl, hair in a bunch) all stand side by side facing roughly towards the viewer/teacher side, bodies front-on or angled slightly. RIGHT panel (after): teal speech bubble from the teacher: 'STATUE!'. Same four children frozen in new facing directions compared with the left panel: A has his BACK to the viewer (facing away); B faces the viewer but turned slightly to the viewer's left (body angled), her hand touches C's arm; C faces the viewer/front (same way as before), one hand raised to his ear; D shows her side (profile) facing the viewer's right. The picture is used to compare each child's final facing direction with the starting one (A = back turned, B = part turn, C = same as start, D = side-on). Labels A, B, C, D appear under the children in both panels.
Second use of P01-scene-1: the same before and after pictures of children A, B, C, D, now with the turn named under each child in the solution (A half turn, B and C full turn, D neither).

Two children (Ashutosh, a boy in khaki shirt and brown shorts, at left; Sahana, a girl in khaki shirt and brown pleated skirt, at right, arms stretched out) stand on a brown ground patch, each with a thin dark ring drawn on the ground around their feet. Ashutosh's ring is a COMPLETE ellipse around both his feet. Sahana's ring is an INCOMPLETE arc (open on the right side, a half-moon shape under her feet). It shows full turn = complete circle and half turn = half circle on the ground. No numbers or labels.

Two round analogue clock faces side by side (coral/salmon rim, white face, numbers 1 to 12, bold tick at 12, 3, 6, 9 and small ticks at the other hours). Each clock has a black arrow from the centre straight up to 12 (the initial position) and a red arrow from the centre. LEFT clock: red arrow points down-right to the 5 (about 145 to 150 degrees clockwise from 12); a blue dashed circle (radius about a third of the clock face, centred on the clock centre, almost a full circle) with a small arrowhead at its end near 11 pointing right/clockwise towards 12, starting just right of 12 and passing clockwise through 3, 5 (it crosses the red hand), 6 and 9. It shows the hand going round the circle and returning to 12. RIGHT clock: black arrow up to 12 and red arrow pointing straight down to 6 (half way round); no dashed circle.

A giant (Ferris) wheel drawn front-on: a large circle (rim) with 24 coloured passenger cabins evenly spaced around the rim (every 15 degrees; colours orange, teal, blue, yellow-green, green in no fixed pattern), thin spokes radiating from the red hub, thin concentric circles inside, two red support legs forming an inverted V down from the hub to the ground, small bushes at the base, a street lamp at the left, a ground line. A circled letter E is printed just above the topmost cabin (the orange cabin at 12 o'clock): this marks the starting position. A girl (Reema, orange kurta, long plait) stands at the bottom right outside the wheel looking at it. The picture is used to count turns of the wheel (full turn = back to E, half turn = bottom, quarter turns = 3 o'clock / 9 o'clock positions).

Table with a blue-green rounded outline, 4 columns and 6 rows (1 header row + 5 object rows). Header row (pink): 'Object' | 'Less than a 1/4 turn' | '1/4 turn' | 'More than a 1/4 turn' (the fraction is printed as a stacked 1 over 4 each time). First column (light green cells), top to bottom: Clothes clip, Door with hinge, Tongs, Scissors, File cover. The other three columns are white and EMPTY in all 5 rows (15 empty cells) for the student to tick. Below the table are two bullet questions with dotted answer lines (names of objects that make a half turn / a full turn).

In a lavender rounded box (left part): two hands each holding one drinking straw; the straws are joined at their lower ends by a paper clip and open up in a V shape: the green-and-white striped straw goes up to the left, the yellow-and-white striped straw goes up to the right, each about 45 degrees from vertical, so they make an angle of about 90 degrees at the clip (bottom, centre). Beside it (middle): the two straws shown separately and nearly parallel: the green striped straw vertical, the yellow striped straw leaning slightly (top tilted a little right), and two paper clips lying below them (one brown, one grey). It models an angle made by turning one straw about a fixed one.

Inside a beige speech bubble, three angles each made of two thin striped straws joined at a corner: (1) 'A right angle' (top right): one straw vertical going up from the corner and one straw horizontal going right, forming an L (90 degrees). (2) 'An acute angle' (left): one straw vertical going up and the other going from the same bottom corner up-right at about 30 degrees above horizontal (angle of about 60 degrees between the straws). The label 'An acute angle' sits below the straws. (3) 'An obtuse angle' (bottom right): one straw vertical going up and the other going down-right at about 45 degrees below horizontal (angle of about 135 degrees); the label 'An obtuse angle' sits to its left. Each picture has its caption text beside or below it. A girl character stands at the left edge of the bubble.

Two thin striped straws lying end to end along one horizontal line (left straw above/overlapping the right one slightly at the join) forming a straight line; a pink dashed curved arrow starts above the middle of the left straw, arcs over to the right and ends with an arrowhead pointing down at the start of the right straw, showing the second straw being turned through a half turn (two quarter turns, 180 degrees). No numbers. A boy character (orange shirt) points at it; his bubble reads 'It is a straight angle.'

Five circled numbered steps drawn in green paper and yellow ice-cream sticks. Step 1: a wide green rectangle (landscape, about 2:1) with 18 vertical dashed fold lines drawn evenly across it (19 equal strips). Step 2: the paper folded like an accordion/zig-zag: about 10 narrow vertical panels with a zig-zag top and bottom edge (5 raised ridges visible). Step 3: the folded paper seen edge-on as a thin vertical green strip. Step 4: the folded paper pinched at the lower-left end and opened a little into two flared halves (upper and lower fan wings); two yellow ice-cream sticks lie crossed at the left, and two red curved arrows labelled 'Paste' (red italic text) point from the sticks to the fan's two halves (one 'Paste' at the upper left, one 'Paste' at the bottom right). Step 5: the finished round fan (green, about 20 radial pleats) with two ice-cream sticks pasted at its centre pointing down (one vertical, one slanting down-right), with yellow ray lines around it (sparkle).

Three round paper fans in a row, each with two ice-cream sticks joined at the fan's centre and a short red arc marking the angle between the two sticks. LEFT fan: one stick pointing straight down, the other pointing down-right (about 30 degrees apart); a small red arc between them at the lower right of the centre (acute). MIDDLE fan: one stick pointing almost straight up (leaning a little right), the other pointing up-left (about 50 to 60 degrees from the first); a red arc across the top-left between them (acute). RIGHT fan: one stick pointing up-left (about 60 degrees left of vertical), the other pointing down and slightly left (about 190 degrees clockwise from vertical); a red arc on the left side between them (about 105 to 110 degrees, obtuse). Fans are green with black radial pleat lines; sticks are yellow; no numbers or labels.

Table with a blue rounded outline, 5 columns and 2 rows. Header row (lavender), left to right: 'Full turn' | '1/2 turn (straight angle)' | '1/4 turn (right angle)' | 'Less than a 1/4 turn (acute angle)' | 'Between a 1/4 and 1/2 turn (obtuse angle)' (fractions stacked). Second row, one picture per column (green paper fan with yellow-brown stick edges): (1) Full turn: fan fully open as a complete circle with one stick pointing straight down from the centre (the two sticks overlap). (2) 1/2 turn: fan open as a half circle, with both sticks forming one horizontal straight line along the bottom (180 degrees). (3) 1/4 turn: fan open as a quarter circle; one stick vertical on the left going up from the corner, the other stick horizontal along the bottom going right (90 degrees, right angle). (4) Less than 1/4 turn: one stick horizontal along the bottom, the other stick rising up-right at about 55 to 60 degrees from the corner, with the fan filling the gap (acute angle). (5) Between 1/4 and 1/2 turn: one stick horizontal along the bottom going right, the other stick going up-left at about 140 degrees from the right-hand stick (about 135 degrees, obtuse angle), with the fan filling the gap.

Three circles in a row (black outline, white), each with a pale beige shaded part, blue dashed radius lines from the centre and a pink dashed curved arrow with an arrowhead inside the shaded part showing a clockwise turn from a vertical start line at 12 o'clock. Circle 1: the top-right quarter shaded (blue dashed vertical line from centre up and blue dashed horizontal line from centre to the right); pink dashed arrow from the top going clockwise to the right, arrowhead near 3 o'clock pointing down. Caption in teal wavy box: 'This shows a 1/4 turn, or a right angle.' Circle 2: the right half shaded (blue dashed vertical diameter); pink dashed arrow from the top going clockwise round to the bottom with arrowhead at the bottom pointing left. Caption: 'This shows a 1/2 turn, or a straight angle.' Circle 3: three quarters shaded (everything except the top-left quarter; blue dashed lines from the centre up and from the centre left); pink dashed arrow from the top going clockwise through right and bottom to the left, arrowhead at the left pointing up. Caption: 'This shows a 3/4 turn, which is more than a straight angle.'

CORRECTED: Eight red marks are drawn on one model house of books (boy and girl are decoration). From the picture, with the solution measure in brackets: A is the wedge at the apex of the yellow gable roof, between the yellow board and the white inner pages (about 115 degrees, obtuse); B is the quarter-circle mark in the gap between the two stacks of upright books, where the right face of the left stack (thin orange book) meets the top of the flat blue book (90 degrees, right); C is the wedge at the apex of the orange A-frame (about 45 degrees, acute); D is the wedge at the lower-left end of the leaning orange board inside the lower box, between the left upright book and the board (about 50 degrees, acute); E is the wedge at the upper-right end of the same board, between the board and the right upright book (about 45 degrees, acute); F is the quarter-circle at the foot of the middle orange upright book under the yellow board, between the book and the ground (right); G is the quarter-circle at the top-left corner of the right orange upright book, under the yellow board (right; the book leans very slightly in the picture); H is the wide wedge on the yellow board just right of the A-frame's right foot, between the board and the leaning book (about 110 degrees, obtuse). The circled letters are lavender discs: A above-right of the roof, B in the gap, C above-right of the A-frame, H above the yellow board, D at the lower left of the lower box, E at the lower middle, F below the middle upright book, G right of the right upright book.
Second use of P04-book_house-3: the same house with the eight marked angles, now named in the solution (A obtuse, B right, C acute, D acute, E acute, F right, G right, H obtuse).

Five horizontal beige rounded rows stacked vertically. In each row: a gymnast in a blue leotard at the left (jumping with arms raised, legs apart), an EMPTY white rectangle in the middle (answer box), and at the right an angle diagram: a black dot as the vertex with two black arrows (open arrowheads at the free ends) and a small red dotted arc at the vertex marking the opening. Row 1: legs close, narrow V; angle diagram vertex at top, two arrows pointing down-left and down-right, about 60 degrees between them (acute). Row 2: legs wider; angle diagram vertex at top, arrows down-left and down-right, about 90 degrees between them (right angle). Row 3: legs wider still; vertex at top, arrows down-left and down-right at about 30 degrees below horizontal, about 120 degrees between them (obtuse). Row 4: legs almost flat; vertex at top, arrows slightly down-left and down-right (about 15 degrees below horizontal), about 150 degrees between them (obtuse). Row 5: full split; the angle diagram is a horizontal straight line with a dot at the centre and arrowheads at both ends, red dotted arc below the dot (180 degrees, straight angle).
Second use of P05-gymnast_angles-1: the same five rows with the empty answer boxes filled in the solution, top to bottom acute, right, obtuse, obtuse, straight.
